dedupe_keys.name: goodd global georeferenced database of dams more than 38 000 dams and catchments

description: GOODD is a global database of more than 38,000 dams digitised by a small team from satellite imagery in Google Earth, together with the catchment of each dam, described in a 2020 data descriptor in Scientific Data. It provides raw digitised coordinates of dam walls, which the authors suggest may be useful for machine learning of dam identification from imagery, and a global vector file of the watershed of each dam; the paper sets out approaches to bias estimation and validation. Coverage is global across all inhabited continents. Access is free as Esri Shapefiles in WGS84, compressed in one zip file on figshare under CC0, and through the Global Dam Watch portal. Caveats: dams carry location and catchment but no attributes such as height, capacity or purpose, only visible dams were digitised, and the dataset has a single 2020 version. Simulation uses: locating dams for flood and dam break exposure, and linking reservoirs to upstream catchments in water supply and hydropower models. Related records: the Global Dam Tracker (data-gdat-global-dam-tracker), GRanD (data-grand-global-reservoir-and-dam-database) and GeoDAR (data-geodar-georeferenced-global-dams-reservoirs).
